newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan rose slightly to 8.2990 against the U.S. dollar on Friday from Thursday's 8.3000, with no impact seen from an announcement on conditions for foreign banks to do local currency business, traders said.
Offical media said on Friday that China would soon allow a handful of foreign banks to conduct business in yuan and gave some details of the conditions under which they would operate.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2994 and moved around 8.2990 for most of the session, hitting an intra-day high of 8.2987 and a low of 8.2995.
Trading was dull, with most done at 8.2990, traders said.
Dealers said the announcement on the foreign banks would have no impact on the yuan's movements in the short term.
"There will still be restrictions on the banks who get approval to do the yuan business," one dealer said.
"It is good news for the yuan in the long term because foreign banks could make the market more active and attractive," a second dealer said.
They expect the yuan to fall below 8.3000 early next week.
The yuan closed slightly up at 7.3350 from 7.3412 against 100 Japanese yen and down slightly at 1.0730 from 1.0725 against the Hong Kong dollar.
